transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

I can’t stop thinking about how my face looks wrong, especially my nose and skin, and it’s really taking over my life. I spend so much time worrying about it every day that it’s hard to focus on work or even want to go out and see people.

Do you find yourself repeatedly checking mirrors, comparing your appearance to others, or spending a lot of time trying to fix or hide these perceived flaws, and if so, about how many hours a day does this take?

Yeah, I’m constantly checking any reflective surface I pass, or zooming in on photos of myself, and then comparing my face to other people’s or celebrities online. I spend a lot of time redoing my makeup, changing outfits, and picking at my skin to “fix” it, and overall it probably adds up to around 3–5 hours a day.

Do you recognize on some level that other people might see your nose and skin as normal or not as bad as you think, or are you completely convinced that they truly look deformed or ugly despite what anyone says?

Most of the time I’m really convinced they look awful and that people must notice, and reassurance doesn’t really change that feeling. I do have occasional moments where I wonder if I’m exaggerating it in my head, but those don’t last long before I go back to believing they look wrong.
Have you ever heard voices or had strong beliefs that others are talking about, laughing at, or plotting against you because of your appearance, even when there’s no clear evidence they are doing so?

I haven’t heard voices or anything like that. I do sometimes feel like people are staring at me or maybe judging how I look, especially my nose and skin, but I know I might be reading into things and I don’t have any solid proof they’re actually talking about me.

When these thoughts about your nose and skin come up, do they feel like unwanted, intrusive thoughts that you try to resist or push away, or do they feel more like a fixed belief that something is definitely wrong with your face that you don’t really question?

It’s mostly a fixed belief that something is definitely wrong with my face, like I just “know” my nose and skin look bad, even if people say otherwise. I do sometimes try to tell myself I’m overreacting or to stop thinking about it, but the thoughts come right back and feel very convincing.

Because of these worries about your nose and skin, do you avoid social situations, work, school, or being seen without makeup or certain clothes, and if so, how much has this actually interfered with your daily life (for example, missing work or canceling plans)?

Yeah, I avoid a lot because of it—I’ve called in sick to work a few times just because I couldn’t stand the idea of people seeing my face, and I cancel plans with friends at least a couple of times a month. I won’t go out without makeup and certain clothes that I feel hide things, and getting ready can take over an hour because I keep redoing everything until it feels “good enough,” which makes me late or I just give up and stay home.

Apart from worrying that your face looks wrong, do you also have other kinds of repetitive, unwanted thoughts (for example about contamination, harm coming to others, needing things to be exactly symmetrical) that make you do specific rituals or routines to feel less anxious?
I don’t really have those kinds of thoughts, it’s almost all about how my face looks. I don’t do any special cleaning, checking, or counting rituals apart from the stuff related to my appearance.

Are you also very worried about your overall body shape or weight, or doing things like strict dieting, excessive exercise, or avoiding food mainly because of how your body looks, or is your concern almost entirely focused on your face (nose and skin)?

It’s almost entirely focused on my face, especially my nose and skin. I do think my body could look better and sometimes feel small or not toned enough, but I’m not doing strict dieting or extreme workouts because of it—my day-to-day obsession is really about my face.

Do you ever spend a lot of time worrying that you have a serious medical illness or physical problem inside your body (like a disease or organ problem), or is your worry almost completely about how your face looks on the outside?

My worry is almost completely about how my face looks on the outside. I don’t really spend time thinking I have some serious illness or internal problem; it’s all about my nose and skin looking wrong.

Have you ever had, or seriously planned to have, cosmetic procedures or surgery on your nose or skin because of these concerns, and if so, what happened and did it actually make you feel any better about your appearance afterward?

Yeah, I’ve had a couple of dermatology treatments for my skin and I’ve had consultations for a nose job, even saved up and almost booked it twice. The skin stuff only made me feel a bit better for a few weeks before I started obsessing again, and with my nose I always end up backing out because I’m scared it won’t fix how I feel or I’ll just find something else wrong.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in physical appearance (nose and skin) that appear minimal or normal to others, spends 3–5 hours per day engaging in repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, comparing, camouflaging, skin picking) driven by these concerns, and experiences clear functional impairment (avoiding work and social activities, prolonged grooming). The focus is on perceived deformity of appearance rather than internal health or classic OCD themes, consistent with body dysmorphic disorder, which in ICD-10 is coded under hypochondriacal disorder (F45.2). Obsessive–compulsive disorder (F42.7) is considered but broader non-appearance-related obsessions/compulsions are absent; the repetitive behaviors are specifically tied to appearance concerns, supporting F45.2 as the primary diagnosis.
